question: How many Lok Sabha seats are there for the state of Meghalaya?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Two**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Two** Lok Sabha seats are allocated to the state of Meghalaya.
 
• The Lok Sabha, also known as the House of the People, is the lower house of India's bicameral Parliament.
 
• Members of the Lok Sabha are directly elected by the people of India, with each state allocated a certain number of seats based on its population.
 
• Meghalaya, being one of the smaller states in terms of population, has two representatives in the Lok Sabha.
 
• The allocation of seats to the states is done according to the provisions of the Constitution of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949** and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written** constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The allocation of Lok Sabha seats is periodically revised based on population changes reflected in the decennial census.
